title: When do stored facts become available in looped transformers?
abstract: arXiv:2611.28808v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Looped transformers do not acquire new knowledge during a forward pass. Prior work shows that they store as many bits in their weights as non-looped models. It remains unclear how recurrence makes this knowledge available during inference. We study this question using synthetic factual recall and multi-hop reasoning, measuring depth-resolved readable information in bits with native readouts and tuned lenses. Under final-loop supervision, single-hop facts become readable progressively: heavier memorization loads delay retrieval despite comparable final readable information. Untied baselines of equal unrolled depth concentrate retrieval near the end of their stacks, whereas looped models expose facts earlier. This delay is not intrinsic to the tested recall tasks: training with supervision and depth-specific readouts at every loop makes near-final information readable after the first loop in all tested configurations. translated_title: 循环Transformer中存储的事实何时变得可用？
translated_abstract: 循环Transformer在前向传播过程中不会获取新知识。先前研究表明，它们在权重中存储的信息量（比特数）与非循环模型相当，然而循环结构如何在推理过程中使这些知识变得可用仍不清楚。我们利用合成的事实回忆与多跳推理任务来研究这一问题，并通过原生读出层和调优透镜以比特为单位测量按深度分辨的可读信息。在最终循环监督下，单跳事实逐步变得可读：尽管最终可读信息量相当，更大的记忆负担会延迟检索。具有相同展开深度的非权重共享基线模型将检索集中在网络堆栈末端附近，而循环模型则更早地暴露事实。这种延迟并非所测试回忆任务所固有的：在所有测试配置中，若在每个循环都施加监督并使用特定深度的读出层进行训练，接近最终的信息在第一次循环后即可读取。表征分析……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文揭示了循环Transformer中存储的事实知识是随循环深度逐步变得可读的，并证明在每个循环都提供监督和深度特定读出层进行训练时，接近最终的信息在第一次循环后即可读取。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals that stored factual knowledge in looped transformers becomes readable progressively across loops, and shows that training with supervision and depth-specific readouts at every loop makes near-final information readable after just the first loop.
